assertions.name: sign_correct_at_both_A
assertions.source: The derived Brunnian cluster has the same sign as the residual it must supply at both A and both levels (A=3 positive, A=4 negative) — the parity sign law derived in PR #4458 holds against the forward AME-model residual. Only the magnitude fails.

assertions.name: shortfall_divergence_exceeds_10x
assertions.source: THE FINDING. If a single missing normalisation explained both A, the cabled shortfall ratio A=4/A=3 would be 1. It is 49.7217 (base level: 109.18), far above 10 — so the shortfall grows sharply with A and no constant re-weight can close both. Any normalisation tuned to close A=4 would break the A=3 near-miss by that same factor, which independently confirms the anti-fit guard on this bean.

description: Bean qou-g3e1, the A=4 Brunnian MAGNITUDE leg. The sign and order are derived exactly (order 6, leading (q-1) coeff -96; PR #4458); this compares the derived cluster magnitude c_A = E_0*(1-tau_A) against the forward residual mu_A (AME - model, never inverted) at BOTH known A and BOTH levels (base band commutator, width-3 cabled). KEY RESULT: the shortfall is NOT constant in A — at the cabled level A=3 is a ~1.59x near-miss while A=4 is ~78.8x short, a ~50x divergence — so NO single constant re-weight can close both, and any normalisation tuned to close A=4 would break the A=3 near-miss by the same factor. Independently confirms the bean's anti-fit guard. Sign is correct at both A. Scope-(a): compares and reports; no re-weighting, no fit, no tuning, nothing wired. All inputs read from committed witnesses.
